sentences.text: By means of the bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.02 of 2024 at Police Station-Amritpur, District-Farrukhabad under Section 376 IPC and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 09.01.2024.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 20.02.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Shailendra Kumar Tripathi, learned counsel holding brief of Shri Karunesh Narayan Tripathi, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Sushant Misra, learned counsel for the informant and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1.
The victim was wrongly shown as a minor of 14 years in the F.I.R. only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.

2.The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The victim in her statements under Sections 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that she is 14 years of age respectively.
(iii) The medical report sent by the Chief Medical Officer, Farrukhabad to determine the age of the victim opines that she is 15 years of age.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim is in fact a major.
Two submissions are made in regard to the aforesaid medical report.
Firstly, the range of error in determining the age is about two years and the same should be read in favour of the applicant at this stage.
Secondly, the relevant scientific parameters as per latest medical protocol which would establish the majority of the victim has been excluded from consideration in the medical report.
The medical report is flawed.
In fact the victim is a major.
3. The applicant has been falsely nominated on account of village rivalry between the parties.
4. Delay of 7 days in lodgement of the F.I.R. in the facts of this case is fatal to the prosecution case.

5. False and aggravated allegations were made by the victim against the applicant in her statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C. and 164 Cr.P.C. at the behest of her parents only to save the failing prosecution case.
6. Prosecution case set out in the submissions of the victim is that on the fateful day, she had gone to work her agricultural fields along with her mother and brother.
Her mother and brother were present in their neighbouring field when the incident happened, and the victim was cutting barsing crop when the applicant dragged her away to his field and raped her.

sentences.text: 7. The victim never raised an alarm.
The victim was armed with a hansiya at the time of the incident.
She never resisted the applicant.
The victim's mother and brother who were in the vicinity too were not alerted to the commotion.
8. Prosecution is inherently false and is liable to be disbelieved.
9. Medical evidence does not corroborate the victim being dragged through the agricultural fields or commission of rape by the applicant with the victim.
10. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
11. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Rajveer be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement rendered by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).

sentences.text: The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Photostat copy of the medical report drawn up by the Chief Medical Officer to determine the age of the victim shall be duly attested and retained by the Registry as part of the records of the Court.
The original medical report, if any, shall be returned to the concerned Chief Judicial Magistrate for onward transmission to the concerned Investigating Officer.
